name: Ditto
sounds_sub: Eight short pieces, each one factory program played as the FM-1 plays it: one sampler, its eight voices, its arpeggiator, delay and reverb. No effects added afterwards.
tagline: An eighties sampler for the M-VAVE FM-1, after the E-mu Emulator II: two sounds layered, eight bits, an analog filter.
lead: The FM-1 as a sampler of the mid-eighties: a library of sixteen sounds, two of them on every note, through the grain of an 8-bit companded sampler into a 24 dB filter, with envelopes, LFOs, a patch bay, an arpeggiator and a step sequencer. Every page draws what it does.

device_sub: Twelve buttons open the sections: EDIT the two sounds and the mixer, SCL the filter, ENV the envelopes, LFO the LFOs and the patch bay, FX the effects. KNOB 1–4 always set the four cards on the screen, ALGORITHM is always the cutoff.
features_sub: One sampler voice, explored in depth, with 32 programs.

features.p: Strings, a choir, an orchestra hit, piano, brass, flute, cellos, organ, harpsichord, marimba, tubular bells, pizzicato, double bass, timpani, a breathy recorder, harp: 41 zones from CC0 recordings. Three slots for your own samples.
SOUND A and SOUND B stacked, crossfaded by the velocity or split at a key, B with its own semitone and tune. A patch cord moves the balance between them.
CHARACTER: EII, 8-bit μ-law and no interpolation, the grain of the Emulator II; EMU 1, 8-bit linear and rougher; or CLEAN, the recordings as they are.
The notes start further into the sample, past its attack; a sustained sound loops while the key is held, or plays once through like tape.
LPF24 after the Emulator II's SSM 24 dB, LPF12, BPF, HPF and MS20, with key tracking and their own envelope.
FILTER EG and AMP EG; two LFOs with key sync and tempo sync; four patch cords from the envelopes, LFOs, velocity or keyboard to pitch, the balance, the cutoff and more. DRIFT ages the clocks.
Ten arp types over 1–4 octaves with latch, swing and steps on/off; a 16-step sequencer with notes, ties, accents and slides, saved with the program.
MOD FX (chorus, flanger, ensemble, phaser, or METAL distortion), a stereo delay in time with the tempo and a reverb, in three orders.
24 factory sounds (STRINGS, CHOIR, ORCH HIT, PIANO, BRASS, SHAKUHACHI, BOW + PLUCK, BASS / PIANO, HIT ARP, AIR CHOIR…) and eight free slots. MIDI Program Change picks them.
SOUND A and SOUND B draw their sample, its loop and START; the filter its curve, the envelopes and LFOs their shapes. A record turns at power-on.
